expectations.name: initial_trip
expectations.detail: triggering event (fault_fired {'slot': 'weld_ssr'}) never occurred [BLOCKED: context_valid is never set true by safety_core_build_input() (firmware/SaftyFW/src/tasks/safety_core.c) -- S3's block lives inside safety_guards.c's context_valid-gated else-branch and is unconditionally reset while context_valid is false, so this cannot fire against present-day SaftyFW.]

blocked_on.reason: context_valid is never set true by safety_core_build_input() (firmware/SaftyFW/src/tasks/safety_core.c) -- S3's block lives inside safety_guards.c's context_valid-gated else-branch and is unconditionally reset while context_valid is false, so this cannot fire against present-day SaftyFW.
blocked_on.phase: Phase 7 (link_task) is built and already publishes this context -- link_task_publish_context()/ link_task_get_context_snapshot() (firmware/SaftyFW/src/tasks/ link_task.c) parse and cache every SAFETY_CMD_PUSH_CONTEXT (0x07) frame today. The real gap is one layer up: safety_core.c's safety_core_build_input() never calls link_task_get_context_snapshot() at all (see its own TODO at safety_core.c:208-210), so context_valid stays at its zero-init false regardless of what the ESP sends. A wiring gap in an already-built producer/consumer pair, not a missing Phase 7 deliverable.
